catalog_citation: Dum-Tragut, Jasmine. 2009. Armenian: Modern Eastern Armenian. (London Oriental and African Language Library 14.) Amsterdam/Philadelphia: John Benjamins.
catalog_quote: In Modern Eastern Armenian, the stress lies on the last syllable with a full vowel-nucleus. The stressed vowel is characterised by greater loudness, higher pitch and (in general) greater lengths. Some examples: girk' "book", grk'í "book, DAT", grk'ér "books", ěnkér "friend", ěnkrój "friend, DAT", ěnkernér "friends" ... In some cases, the stress lies on the penultimate syllable: – If the vowel contained in the last closed syllable is the schwa [ə], as in káysr, ástł – In some words, the stress is on the penultimate rather than on the last syllable, e.g. órewě "any", núynisk "even" ... – If the last consonant of a word is represented by a definite article-suffix -ě, or -n, possessive suffix -s-, -d, e.g. całíkě [tsałíkə] "the flower" ... In some cases, the stress falls on other than the ultimate full vowel syllable: – In some loan words, especially proper names, a non-final syllable is st…
sweep_summary: Two title-hits for Eastern Armenian, neither obtainable. (1) Skopeteas 2021 is an unpublished Bielefeld/Göttingen manuscript on focus and question intonation (prosody, not stress placement); no copy exists in any index or repository reached, and its content is known only second-hand through Seyfarth et al. 2024 (JIPA, on file) and its published successor Chakmakjian, Dolatian & Skopeteas 2024 (Speech Prosody, on file, 'confirms'). (2) Dolatian 2021a (NLLT 39: 843-886) is closed access; Springer serves only a preview (abstract silent on stress placement; a footnote mentions that high vowels lack secondary stress), and Springer's PDF is blocked by a JS challenge; no repository copy. The sweep did yield one new open first-hand statement, from the Glossa article that cites both items: Dolatian 2022 (Glossa 7(1), p. 7), 'Stress is on the rightmost non-schwa vowel in the prosodic word (Vaux 1998; Dolatian 2021a)', which confirms the catalog's fixed-strict coding but does not supersede Dum-Tragut 2009 (or the already-held Seyfarth et al. 2024 description).

new_statements.reading: Primary stress is fixed on the last non-schwa vowel of the prosodic word (final syllable unless its nucleus is schwa, in which case the preceding full vowel); clitics are outside the stress domain. The statement is generic to standard Armenian (paper covers Western and Eastern lects) and is illustrated on Western Armenian forms; it agrees with the catalog's fixed-strict coding.
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding Dum-Tragut 2009 quotation is verbatim in the held extracted text at line 2560 under '1.4.1 Stress' (PDF p. 64), with the continuation bullets on PDF p. 65 and the secondary-stress sentence at lines 2656-2657, matching the stated locator. (2) Deciding source is a 2009 760-pp reference grammar, the best-ranked description in Glottolog, seconded by Vaux's phonology (1994 diss., now fetched sources; 1998 OUP not held). A web search for newer stress/prosody work found the 2024 JIPA Illustration (Seyfarth et al.), a 2024 Speech Prosody production study (Chakmakjian et al.), and the 2023 LangSci grammar of Iranian Armenian; all three were fetched sources to and all state the same rule: stress on the rightmost non-schwa (full) vowel, penult when the final nucleus is schwa, clitics unstressed -- i.e. they confirm the fixed/unbounded 'las

sources.quote: 'Iranian Armenian seems to utilize the same lexical stress system as Standard Eastern Armenian ... Within the morphological word, stress is generally final on the rightmost non-schwa vowel ... If the final syllable has a schwa, then stress is on the penultimate syllable ... Besides final schwas, stress is avoided on clitics.' Irregular: negation prefix and ordinal suffixes.

sources.citation: Chakmakjian, Samuel, Hossep Dolatian & Stavros Skopeteas. 2024. Word stress and prosodic events in Eastern Armenian. Proc. Speech Prosody 2024 (Leiden), pp. 1170-1174. ISCA Archive.
sources.quote: 'Word stress is generally final in EA/WA, falling on the rightmost non-schwa vowel. Stress is not final with (a) word-final schwa, compare final stress in [zɑteˈlu] 'of choosing' and penult stress in [zɑˈtelə] 'the choosing', and (b) certain suffixes falling outside the stress domain.' 10-speaker production study; nuclear H* aligns with the stressed syllable.
